name: Rishi Sunak
role: Former prime minister of the United Kingdom
description: British prime minister assessed through the 2022–2024 government and 2024 election programme.

axes.brief: Parliamentary elections and constitutional executive accountability were retained, including conceding the 2024 election.
axes.counter: The Rwanda legislation overrode a court’s factual assessment through parliamentary statute, not an unlimited personal executive veto. Binding recall and referendums are qualified.

axes.brief: Expanded protest restrictions, policing and border enforcement alongside civil criticism and judicial safeguards.
axes.counter: Security emphasis does not abolish warrants or every court review; moral censorship and bulk movement records are modern estimates.

axes.brief: Shared British civic identity, English integration and common institutions were emphasised alongside recognition of minority communities.
axes.counter: His Hindu identity and participation in plural celebrations do not imply clerical government or rejection of a shared national culture.

axes.brief: Reducing net migration, tighter dependent visas and the Rwanda asylum scheme prioritised control and eligibility.
axes.counter: Legal family and skilled routes and some refugee schemes remained; broad permanent refugee admission regardless of compatibility is qualified downward.

axes.brief: Supported Ukraine militarily, NATO, defence spending and deterrence, with professional armed forces.
axes.counter: 2024 national-service proposal included civilian options; neither universal male military conscription nor autonomous lethal AI was established.

axes.brief: Post-Brexit national policy, border and monetary control coexisted with NATO, trade agreements and treaty cooperation.
axes.counter: Continued European human-rights commitments qualify blanket external-jurisdiction rejection; voluntary alliances differ from political federation.

axes.brief: Private enterprise and private service provision were favoured while the NHS, BBC and public infrastructure were retained.
axes.counter: No wholesale privatisation of hospitals or rail infrastructure was his programme; emergency/public banks do not imply a general state commercial sector.

axes.brief: Post-Brexit trade agreements and open investment were promoted.
axes.counter: Food security, strategic ownership screening and subsidy responses create exceptions; imports were not to be protected across the whole economy.

axes.brief: Market allocation and business investment were normal, with minimum-wage rules, targeted support and industrial priorities.
axes.counter: The energy crisis and strategic sectors prompted subsidy and intervention; an independent central bank remained part of the framework.

axes.brief: Tax reductions, welfare conditionality and targeting benefits were emphasised.
axes.counter: Progressive income-tax rates and the safety net remained; not every wealth or inheritance tax was abolished and tax cuts were fiscally constrained.

axes.brief: Civil policy without religious approval, plural faith recognition and state courts were supported.
axes.counter: Established church, religious holidays, faith schools and bishops in the Lords were not wholly removed; personal Hindu belief is not the axis itself.

axes.brief: Traditional family, sex-based institutional safeguards and parental influence received emphasis.
axes.counter: Same-sex marriage was legal and accepted, women’s careers were normal and tradition was not an all-purpose veto on reform.

axes.brief: AI investment, infrastructure and technological solutions were promoted alongside an AI safety summit and existing clinical safeguards.
axes.counter: Net-zero delays and energy development do not establish support for unchecked brain implants or embryo enhancement.

axes.brief: Devolved administrations and local delivery persisted within parliamentary sovereignty and a unified national framework.
axes.counter: Opposed a further Scottish independence referendum; devolution does not mean regional constitutions or councils can alter powers unilaterally.

axes.brief: Schooling, skills and opportunity were emphasised as ways to improve outcomes.
axes.counter: Policy emphasis is weak evidence on comparative biological causation; no racial IQ or violence explanation is attributed without a direct statement.
